limitations: P1 — Counterevidence: Equation(20) retains correct edge indexing; corrected whole-state finite-increment kernel tends to it. Thus neither limiting derivative formula nor final theorem is refuted. A multiset reading would change explicit G definition and would not cure untouched-herd term.
P2 — Counterevidence: Replacing minimum by maximum M=max_[0,1]F gives valid bound. Restricting integral to[1,t-1] gives lengtht-2>=t/3 for t>=3. Large-time strict-monotonicity strategy can survive.
P3 — Counterevidence: Usingm=ceil(t_x), thresholdx/m yieldsm^(p+2)x^(-p-1)times the uniformincrementmoment; forx>=e same logarithmic order, boundedx harmless. Final moment conclusion not refuted.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.

proposition.claim:
Fix an integer \(d\geq3\), birth rate \(\lambda>0\), and splitting rate \(v>0\). A herd shape \(A\) is any finite nonempty subset of the infinite \(d\)-regular tree. It need not be connected (Definition 2.1, p. 756). A state \(\xi\in\mathcal S\) is a finite multiset of such shapes. For an edge \(e\), write \(A_{e,1},A_{e,2}\) for the portions on the two sides of \(e\). An edge is active precisely when both portions are nonempty.

Equation reference: gen. Definition 2.3, p. 757, gives a death rate of one per particle, birth rate \(\lambda\) per occupied-neighbor arrow to an unoccupied site of the same herd, and split rate \(v\) per active edge per herd copy. Different herds evolve independently, even when their spatial locations overlap. Let \(X(\xi)\) be the total particle count, \(H(\xi)\) the total number of occupied adjacent pairs within herds, and \(\mathcal E(\xi)\) the active-edge count with herd multiplicities. Let \(L_v\) denote this generator and put \[S_v(t)\xi=\mathbb E_{\lambda,v}[X_t\mid\Xi_0=\xi],
 \qquad F_v(t)=S_v(t)\delta_{\{o\}}.\] Splitting preserves \(X\). Counting the available birth arrows gives \[
 L_vX=(d\lambda-1)X-2\lambda H .\] The paper’s pure-birth domination and Corollary 2.3 provide finite moments on bounded time intervals. Proposition 2.7 implies \(F_v(t+s)\leq F_v(t)F_v(s)\). These facts supply the integrability and positivity used below; in particular, \(F_v(t)\geq e^{-t}>0\), by survival of the initial particle.

Successor-state sums with m(xi,xi')=xi(A) equal elementary-edge sums; positive-epsilon equation(29) cancels untouched herds.

d integer>=3; lambda>0; v>0; epsilon>0 for finite increment; finite nonempty herd shapes, not necessarily connected; finite herd multiset; t>=0.

repair.content:
Keep each active-edge event; use whole-state S_(v+epsilon)(xi-delta_A+split)-S_v(xi). Bound absolute kernel by2exp(dlambdaT)X E, allowing existing bounded-time moment domination.

gamma=q/M whereq positive finite clock-event probability; finite-time joint continuity preserves continuous parameter dependence. Restrict time domain as above.

Use ceiling and bound only large x when assertingO(logx).
